question: Where these instruments require a record of what an automated system did, do they require that record to say who authorised a consequential action, and to be checkable by somebody other than the party that produced it?
why: A deployer will be obliged to keep records before anybody has said what a record must contain for it to answer a question afterwards. If the obligation arrives without that, every deployer satisfies it with a log that cannot be checked, and the first time anyone finds out is a claim or an incident.

method.how: Each instrument was read in its published text and searched for four requirements. Every count below was run over the whole document set named for that subject, and every quotation is from it.
method.kinds: Instruments are not the same kind of thing, and a question outside a subject's kind resolves to not applicable rather than absent. A governance framework that deliberately specifies no controls is not failing to specify one, in the same way a vector store is not failing to gate an action.
method.limits: Four questions, not an assessment of whether any of these is good at what it is for. Public text only: ISO/IEC 42001 is paywalled and was not read, which is recorded rather than guessed. No subject was contacted, and this is not a certification of anybody.
method.disputing: Every verdict names the document and the clause, control or criterion it rests on. A wrong one is wrong in a way a pull request can fix.

verdicts.required: The instrument requires it of the party it binds.
verdicts.partial: Required for something adjacent, or required without being checkable.
verdicts.absent: Not required anywhere in the text read.
verdicts.not_applicable: Outside the kind of instrument this is.

questions.text: Is a record of consequential events required at all?
Must that record identify the person who authorised a consequential action?
Must the record be capable of being shown unaltered by somebody other than the party that produced it?

subjects.name: EU AI Act

Q1.note: Article 12(1): high-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system. Article 12(2) gives the purpose as ensuring a level of traceability of the functioning of the system.

Q2.note: Required for one category and for no other, which is the more interesting finding and corrects an earlier reading of this file that said absent. Article 12(3)(d) obliges the logging capabilities of a remote biometric identification system under Annex III point 1(a) to provide the identification of the natural persons involved in the verification of the results, referring to Article 14(5), which requires the action to be separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons with the necessary competence, training and authority. So the legislator wrote this requirement, knew how to word it, and scoped it to a single row of Annex III. For every other high-risk system Article 12(2) asks only for events relevant to three named purposes and specifies no content at all, and nothing in Articles 12, 14 or 26 requires the identity of a person who authorised an action.

Q3.note: No occurrence of tamper, unaltered, integrity of the log, or independent verification in the three articles. The logs must exist and be kept; nothing requires that a kept log can be shown to be the one that was written.

Q4.note: Article 26(6): deployers shall keep the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in Union or national law.

subjects.finding: The obligation everything else is preparing for names the identity of the verifying persons once, for remote biometric identification, and asks every other high-risk system only for events relevant to three purposes with no content specified. The requirement exists, fully drafted, applied to one row of Annex III. Nothing anywhere in these articles requires that a kept log can be shown to be the one that was written.

subjects.name: ForHumanity
subjects.kind: certification scheme, binary criteria applied by auditors
subjects.read: CORE AAA System Governance Deployer v1.6, EU AI Act Multi AAA Agent Governance v1.5, Provider v1.5, Deployer v1.6, and the Guidance on Supporting AAA System Procurement v1.0
subjects.source: pinned in the #euregs and #main_forhumanity channels of the ForHumanity Slack

Q1.note: EM-EU-PR-RK-AC-2602-001 establishes Event Logs across twelve areas including the orchestration layer, outcomes, a risk log and a human interactions log. Roughly 1,300 uses of log across the five documents.

Q2.note: The Event Log is defined as five components paraphrased from ISO 27001:2002: user ID, system activity, date and time, device and location, and IP address. That answers which session acted. Natural person appears 49 times and who approved none; the single occurrence of approver is a plan creator and plan approver in an unrelated criterion.

Q3.note: Data Integrity is defined from NIST as data not altered in an unauthorised manner, and Integrity as the degree to which a system prevents unauthorised access or modification. Both are prevention, and both are used only in Test Data curation, where Data Integrity/Chain-of-custody is a step in the Data Curation Report. No criterion requires that a retained Event Log be shown not to have been altered.

Q4.note: EM-EU-PR-RK-AC-2602-005 requires retention according to the relevant legal framework, and failing that, no less than six months.

subjects.finding: The most developed record-keeping of the four, and the integrity vocabulary is present and defined. It is spent on training data rather than on the log of what the system did.

subjects.name: CoSAI Risk Map
subjects.read: risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml and risks.yaml at main, 35 controls

Q1.note: controlAgentObservability, in full: ensure an agent's actions, tool use, and reasoning are transparent and auditable through logging, allowing for debugging, security oversight, and user insights into agent activity.

Q2.note: No occurrence of approver, who approved, or the identity of the person across the 35 controls. controlComponentIdentityProvenance requires a calling component to verify the callee is the currently registered, non-revoked principal, which is machine identity rather than the person who allowed an action.

Q3.note: controlModelAndDataExecutionIntegrity requires limiting and immutably recording all modifications to runtime AI system components. Immutable recording is therefore required, of configuration changes rather than of the action record. No control requires the action or decision log to be shown unaltered.

Q4.note: No retention requirement in the controls.

subjects.finding: The one instrument here that is actively closing the gap. riskDeceptiveAgentReporting, filed on 6 September 2026, states the distinction directly: the audit trail is intact and what is false is the content of the report. It is open at the time of reading.

subjects.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0
subjects.kind: governance framework, specifies no controls by design

Q1.note: The framework organises risk management into GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE and does not specify controls. It discusses transparency 33 times and accountability 22 times, and contains no occurrence of log, logging, record-keeping or audit trail. That is a property of what the document is for, not a deficiency in it. The companion Playbook carries the suggested actions and is a separate document, not read here.

Q2.note: Not applicable for the same reason. A document that specifies no record cannot specify what goes in one, and the framework names accountability as an outcome to be achieved rather than a field to be written. Accountable appears 22 times and never as a requirement to record who acted.

Q3.note: Not applicable for the same reason. Integrity appears in the framework as a property of a trustworthy AI system, alongside validity and reliability, rather than as a property required of a record. No control could be absent because none is specified.

Q4.note: Not applicable for the same reason. Retention of anything is a control, and the framework specifies none. The Playbook and the organisation's own policy are where a period would be set.

subjects.finding: Included to be counted out. A framework that deliberately specifies no controls cannot be assessed for one, and reporting its zero as a finding would be the error this reading exists to avoid.

subjects.name: AIUC-1
subjects.kind: certification scheme, controls audited by an accredited third party
subjects.read: The published control set, six families and 51 live controls (A 8, B 10, C 12, D 4, E 15, F 2), plus the per-control evidence requirements
subjects.source: https://aiuc-1.com, published without registration; read at https://machinetestimony.org/aiuc-1/

Q1.note: E015, Log AI system activity, is mandatory and applied every 12 months: "Maintain logs of AI system processes, actions, and agent outputs where permitted to support incident investigation, auditing, and explanation of AI system behavior." E009 separately requires third-party API connections, sessions and data access to be logged.

Q2.note: E015.2, the agent-specific logging evidence, requires structured logs capturing "approver identity, timestamp, decision outcome" for authorization events, the standard's own worked example being human-in-the-loop approvals. THE ONLY SUBJECT IN THIS CENSUS THAT ANSWERS REQUIRED HERE. The placement is worth stating: across 51 controls this sub-requirement is the only place a named human is asked for, and C007, the control that establishes human review, is marked Optional and asks for workflow documentation showing assignments rather than reviewers. So the approver is collected as log content rather than established as an oversight duty.

Q3.note: E015.4 requires log integrity protection by name: "write-once-read-many (WORM) storage configuration, cryptographic hashing of log entries, append-only database settings." Further than any other subject here goes. It stays partial because every one of those is held and operated by the party that produced the log, and a digest a deployer computes over its own records and keeps itself does not let anybody else show them unaltered. An auditor inspects the configuration; nothing in the record is checkable by a reader who was not given access.

Q4.note: E015.3 requires log storage evidence including "retention period settings and PII-masking, access control configuration showing who can view logs". The control requires a retention period to be configured and evidenced and states no period of its own, so what is required is that the deployer have an answer rather than that the answer be any particular one.

subjects.finding: The first instrument read by this project that requires the approver's identity, and it is not a law. A private certification scheme with an accredited auditor asks for what the EU AI Act, ForHumanity and CoSAI do not. It also goes furthest on integrity and still stops at controls the producing party operates, which is the same boundary every other subject reaches by a different route.

not_read.name: ISO/IEC 42001
not_read.why: The text is paywalled. A reading whose rule is that a verdict cites the clause it rests on cannot cite what it has not read, and the most widely referenced AI management standard cannot be checked by the deployers it governs without paying for it. That is recorded as a fact about the field rather than assessed as a verdict.
